title: Consider it arranged
lede: The difference between a good week and a great one is usually a handful of details. A chef, a table, a boat, a babysitter — one message and they are handled.
image_alt: A shaded dining terrace at an Ibiza villa

sections.title: One number, for everything
paragraphs: Before you arrive we will ask a few questions: who is coming, what you like to eat, whether you want to be busy or do nothing at all. Then we make the week work around that.

During your stay there is one number to call. It reaches a person, not a portal. If the pool needs attention, a flight is delayed or you decide at four o'clock that you want a table for ten at eight, we will sort it.

sections.title: The things that make a week

items.title: A chef at the villa
items.text: Breakfast, a long lunch, a birthday dinner — with the shopping, the service and the washing up included.

items.title: Tables worth the drive
items.text: From toes-in-the-sand lunches to the island's best dining rooms, booked before you land.

items.title: Boat days
items.text: Day boats, llaüts and crewed yachts, with a skipper who knows where to anchor.

items.title: Wellness
items.text: A trainer at the villa, a massage after the beach, a yoga teacher for the group.

items.title: Children
items.text: Babysitters, nannies and activities that keep everyone happy — including the parents.

items.title: Celebrations
items.text: Birthdays, anniversaries and small weddings, from the cake to the string quartet.

items.title: Transfers & drivers
items.text: Airport transfers, drivers by the evening, cars delivered to the villa.

items.title: The house
items.text: Extra housekeeping, a private bartender, flowers on arrival, the fridge stocked before you get there.

sections.title: Tell us how you like your days
sections.text: Send us a note before you arrive and we will build the week around it — or leave it entirely open and decide as you go.
